groups.title: Passive foundation and valid active Sources
groups.proposal: Build a passive Result only from an active VNC with a specific object, promote that object, remove the source subject completely, and use the licensed nonactive stem.
groups.writingJob: Validate the active Source, reject intransitive and nonspecific-only Sources, delete the active subject, promote the selected specific object from objective to nominative, and replace the active stem with its nonactive Result.
groups.readingJob: Show the active-to-passive transformation, the promoted participant, the deleted source subject, and why a named agent requires an active Nahuatl clause.
groups.decisionSplit: The user supplies the intended active Source and requests passive voice; the application determines eligibility and performs deletion, promotion, case change, and nonactive-stem selection. No agent-retention choice is valid.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse Source, object, and voice controls; do not ask the user to choose case, delete the source subject, retain an agent, or substitute impersonal voice.

groups.title: Passive formula and single-object promotion
groups.proposal: For one specific projective object, move its person and number into the passive subject positions, including a grammatically present silent third-person object, and generate the ordinary intransitive passive formula.
groups.writingJob: Promote the sole specific projective object to subject, preserve its person and number, discard every trace of the source subject, and recognize a typed silent third-person object as a real promotable object.
groups.readingJob: Show the source object and passive subject side by side, explain why different active subjects collapse to the same passive, and make silent-object presence visible without inventing a surface morph.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended active object when composing the Source; once passive is requested, the sole eligible object promotes automatically. A silent versus sounded third-person realization is derived from the Source, not chosen again.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse object-person, number, and voice controls plus clickable formula positions; do not add promotion, nominative-case, deleted-agent, or silent-object-presence switches.

groups.title: Reflexive passive and retained ne
groups.proposal: Promote a specific reflexive object to the passive subject while automatically retaining shuntline ne as the reflexive trace, which makes the passive Result transitive.
groups.writingJob: Convert the source mainline reflexive object into the matching passive subject and place ne in the shuntline object position without losing the reflexive relation.
groups.readingJob: Show the former reflexive object in its new subject positions and identify ne as the retained reflexive relation rather than a second independent participant.
groups.decisionSplit: The user composes a reflexive active Source and requests passive voice; promotion and ne retention are automatic. Reflexive versus reciprocal remains a real Source interpretation choice only where the plural Source permits both.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the familiar reflexive or reciprocal Source choice and passive voice; do not add retain-ne, passive-transitivity, or relocation controls.

groups.title: Reflexive plus projective double-object passive
groups.proposal: When the Source has one reflexive and one specific projective object, promote the projective object and convert the reflexive object to shuntline ne.
groups.writingJob: Identify the projective object as the passive subject, relocate its person and number, convert the source reflexive object to ne, and discard the source subject.
groups.readingJob: Show which object promotes, which becomes ne, and why the passive Result remains transitive.
groups.decisionSplit: The typed Source roles determine the transformation; the user does not choose which of these unlike objects promotes.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the two Source-object specifications and passive voice; add no promotion-target or ne controls.

groups.title: Two specific objects and mainline promotion
groups.proposal: For two specific projective objects, promote the typed mainline object and preserve the shuntline object, including its licensed silent or third-plural realization.
groups.writingJob: Use typed mainline and shuntline authority, promote only the mainline object, retain the shuntline object's person and number, and realize its licensed sounded or silent form.
groups.readingJob: Show mainline promotion, shuntline retention, silent-object number ambiguity, and any third-plural shuntline change after promotion.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses object roles only when composing an actually ambiguous two-object Source; passive generation then follows those roles automatically and preserves real silent-number ambiguity.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the active two-object composition controls and derived role cues; do not ask again which object promotes after the Source is fixed.

groups.title: Specific plus nonspecific and three-object Sources
groups.proposal: Promote the only specific object regardless of line status, retain every nonspecific object unchanged, and apply the same typed rules recursively to licensed three-object Sources.
groups.writingJob: Find the sole eligible specific object, promote it, retain tē or tla and any other licensed object relation, and apply the established transformation without a special three-object shortcut.
groups.readingJob: Show why specificity controls promotion here, preserve genuine role or gloss ambiguity, and display each retained object relation.
groups.decisionSplit: The user resolves only a genuine Source-role or interpretation ambiguity; the application selects the sole specific promotion target and recursively preserves the remaining objects.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse typed object roles and interpretations; do not add promote-mainline, promote-shuntline, retain-tē, retain-tla, or three-object-mode switches.

groups.title: Passive wishes, commands, exhortations, and admonitions

groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended sentence force; the application keeps the passive grammar and derives the compatible form.
